verdict.rationale: Cal.com publishes first-party source under the MIT license through Cal.diy in its official calcom GitHub org, and its own llms.txt markets this self-hostable MIT edition. However, Cal.diy is a fork with all enterprise/commercial code removed (Teams, Organizations, Insights, Workflows, SSO/SAML), and community reports describe Cal.com's move to closed source, so the full product's source is not openly readable. Missing for 10: the main Cal.com product's source under an open license, and coverage of enterprise features (teams, orgs, workflows, SSO) in the open edition.
